answer: The shell warden measures every conch at the market and enters its length in the tally, so only shells of the legal size are sold. A ember shell taken before its season fails the tally: at the atlas of the lip the shell must show the growth the warden's own measure expects, and an undersized shell is seized on the spot. Buying a false tally costs a forger 6,900 in bribes to the warden and fees to the market, and the yarrow book in the market office is kept for five years, so a shell whose measure was never entered is thrown back.
